text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. Developers regularly merge their code changes into a shared repository. Each time this happens, an automated build is triggered to check that the new code works correctly with the existing project. As part of this process, the system runs tests automatically to find any problems. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious. CI pipelines organise these steps, from building to testing and sometimes deploying. By using CI, teams can work faster, reduce bugs, and deliver more reliable software to users.
